privacy: no account numbers, names, free-text details or tokens; row ids hashed; BIC8 codes are synthetic

rules.title: PARTICIPANT_COUNT equals the number of known BICs in the path
rules.plain: A record supports R6 when PARTICIPANT_COUNT equals the count of BIC8 entries in BIC8_PATH that are not '...'.

sample.method: deterministic hash order (hash(rid + 2026)), first rows taken; approximately uniform over the eligible rows

rules.title: CONTINUITY_QFLAG = 'N' exactly when the path contains '...'
rules.plain: Supports R7 when the flag is N and the path has a hidden hop, or the flag is Y and it has none.

sample.method: deterministic hash order (hash(rid + 2026)), first rows taken; approximately uniform over the eligible rows

rules.title: Direct ⇔ exactly 2 participants
rules.plain: Supports when TRANSACTION_TYPE_CODE is Direct and PARTICIPANT_COUNT = 2, or non-Direct and PARTICIPANT_COUNT > 2.

sample.method: deterministic hash order (hash(rid + 2026)), first rows taken; approximately uniform over the eligible rows

rules.title: FX conversions = home-currency changes along the path
rules.plain: Walk the known BICs; map each to its country's home currency; count adjacent changes. Supports C2 when that count equals CURRENCY_CONVERSION_COUNT. The 2 contradicting rows are the only payments in the dataset touching an Eritrean bank: Eritrea never sends, so its home currency is unobservable (shown missing in route_currencies) and the prediction undercounts by exactly one border.

sample.method: deterministic hash order (hash(rid + 2026)), first rows taken; approximately uniform over the eligible rows

rules.title: Payment currency is one of the route banks' home currencies
rules.plain: Supports C3 when CURRENCY_CODE is the home currency of at least one bank on the path. Contradicting records use an outside 'vehicle' currency.

sample.method: deterministic hash order (hash(rid + 2026)), first rows taken; approximately uniform over the eligible rows

rules.title: Path endpoints equal the header BICs (each replaced independently w.p. ≈5%)
rules.plain: Supports the 'unchanged' branch when the first known path BIC equals ORDERING_BIC8 and the last equals BENEFICIARY_BIC8. Contradicting records are the ≈5% replacements the rule predicts — exceptions inside the rule, not failures of it.

condition.supports: list_filter(string_split(path,';'), x -> x <> '...')[1] = obic AND list_filter(string_split(path,';'), x -> x <> '...')[-1] = bbic

sample.method: deterministic hash order (hash(rid + 2026)), first rows taken; approximately uniform over the eligible rows

rules.title: IBAN country prefix equals the bank's BIC country
rules.plain: Among IBAN-formatted ordering accounts, supports P2 when the 2-letter IBAN prefix equals the ordering bank's country. Only the prefix is shown, never the account.

sample.method: deterministic hash order (hash(rid + 2026)), first rows taken; approximately uniform over the eligible rows

rules.title: Long-route tail: K ~ Geometric(1/e) predicts ≈3 rows with ≥ 17 participants
rules.plain: All rows with PARTICIPANT_COUNT ≥ 17. The rule predicts 10M·e^-15 ≈ 3.1; the records below are the complete set.

sample.method: deterministic hash order (hash(rid + 2026)), first rows taken; approximately uniform over the eligible rows

rules.title: Fat-finger amounts sit ≈ two decades from the A1 expectation
rules.plain: Among FAT_FINGER_MISTAKE rows, supports X3 when |log10(amount / A1 baseline)| > 1.3. Contradicting rows are fat-finger labels whose amount looks ordinary — the label overlaps normal noise.

sample.method: deterministic hash order (hash(rid + 2026)), first rows taken; approximately uniform over the eligible rows

rules.title: Duplicate payments repeat amount, path and duration within 2 hours
rules.plain: DUPLICATE_PAYMENT rows. A record supports X2 when another labelled row shares its amount, path and duration within 7,200 s.

condition.supports: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM t t2 WHERE t2.anom='DUPLICATE_PAYMENT' AND t2.rid<>t.rid AND t2.amt=t.amt AND t2.path=t.path AND t2.dur=t.dur AND abs(t2.epoch-t.epoch)<=7200)

sample.method: deterministic hash order (hash(rid + 2026)), first rows taken; approximately uniform over the eligible rows
